question: Under PM-KMY, the monthly pension after 60 years is:
solution:
The correct answer is __**₹3,000**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Pradhan Mantri Kisan Maan-Dhan Yojana (PM-KMY) is a pension scheme launched by the Government of India to provide old-age financial security to small and marginal farmers.
 
• Under PM-KMY, eligible farmers receive a fixed monthly pension of ₹3,000 after attaining the age of 60 years.
 
• The scheme is voluntary and contributory, requiring farmers to contribute a specified amount monthly based on their age, which is matched by an equal contribution from the Government of India.
 
• Small and marginal farmers between the age group of 18 to 40 years are eligible for this scheme, provided they own less than 2 hectares of cultivable land.
 
• The scheme is implemented through the Life Insurance Corporation of India (LIC), which acts as the pension fund manager and ensures timely pension payouts.
 
• Farmers can enroll in the scheme through Common Service Centers (CSCs) spread across India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **₹1,000:**

 
 
• This pension amount corresponds to other smaller pension schemes for certain sections of workers, but it is not the fixed pension under PM-KMY.
 
• ₹1,000 monthly pensions can be observed under schemes for unorganized workers with lower contributions.
 
 
 
• **₹2,000:**
 
 
• There is no provision for a ₹2,000 monthly pension under PM-KMY. The scheme explicitly offers ₹3,000 monthly pensions.
 
• However, ₹2,000 pensions can be a part of other contributory schemes for different segments like small traders or self-employed workers.
 
 
 
• **₹5,000:**
 
 
• ₹5,000 monthly pensions are not applicable under PM-KMY.
 
• Higher pension amounts are generally observed in schemes requiring larger contributions, such as private pension plans or special government schemes for higher-income groups.
 
 
 
• **Main Theme:**
 
 
• The Pradhan Mantri Kisan Maan-Dhan Yojana (PM-KMY) was introduced to provide social security and financial stability to farmers during their old age.
 
• The scheme aims to empower small and marginal farmers by ensuring regular income post-retirement, addressing their vulnerability during non-working years.
 
• PM-KMY complements other farmer welfare schemes such as PM-KISAN, which provides direct income support to farmers.
